2. This appeal arises out of the judgment and decree dated 17.8.98 passed by the learned Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna in Artha Rin Case No. 10 of 1998 decreeing the suit for an amount of Tk. 13,68,768.00. 

 3. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned judgment and decree dated 17.8.98 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna the petitioner has filed the present appeal before this Court. 

 5. Section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat, 1990 provides that an appeal can be taken against a judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat before the High Court Division within 30 days of the decree on depositing in the Court at least 50% of the decretal dues. It appears that instead of depositing 50% of the decretal dues in the Court decreeing the suit, the appellant petitioner deposited the said money in the Current Account of the appellant maintained with the plaintiff bank meant for the purpose. This appears to us that this is a mere technical fault, causing no prejudice to the decree-holder bank and no violence to the spirit of the law. In the facts of the case, we are inclined to hold it as a valid deposit as a condition precedent for filing the appeal before the Court. 

 6. The provision for payment of 50% of the decretal dues before filing an appeal to the High Court Division against any decree passed by an Artha Rin Adalat has been made as a means for prompt realization of a substantial amount of the decretal dues so that a financial institution is not made to wait indefinitely in realizing its dues. It has consistently been held by this Court that procedures laid down for substantive laws are for advancement of the cause of justice and these are never intended to obstruct the course of justice at any rate. We are, therefore, required to look into the substance of the law, rather than its Since the appellant has already substantially complied with the requirement of law by making deposit of 50% of the decretal dues, it will totally unjust and inequitable to adjudge the appellant non suited on a technical knock-out. We are, therefore, of the view that literal technicality cannot be allowed to stand in the way of justice.
